**Palantir Technologies Inc. — FY2024 (year ended December 31, 2024), Form 10-K filed for report_end 2024-12-31**

**How it scales within accounts.** Palantir's stated model is to land on a customer's hardest problem and then widen the footprint inside the same institution. The 10-K says its sales and marketing strategies "allow us to scale existing customer contracts horizontally to include additional divisions or functions within a single institution and vertically to include additional users and user groups," and that by "tackling the customer's most pressing and challenging problems first, we establish the trust needed to expand platform usage across the full enterprise" (chunk 1321655/pltr-20241231:30400). Management also states that "increasing the size and number of the deployments of our existing customers is a major part of our growth strategy" (chunk :60800). AIP bootcamps, introduced into the customer-acquisition process beginning in 2023, are described as accelerating these discussions (chunk :22400).

**Evidence that expansion is actually happening.** The clearest quantitative support is the top-20 customer metric: average revenue from the top twenty customers was **$64.6 million** in the TTM ended December 31, 2024, up **18%** from **$54.6 million** in the TTM ended December 31, 2023 — a growth rate the company itself attributes to "our expanding relationships with existing customers" (chunk :363200; also :22400). My calculation from those two disclosed figures gives 18.3%, consistent with the disclosed 18%.

Revenue growth also came disproportionately from the installed base: of the $347.4 million government revenue increase, **$280.7 million** came from government customers existing as of December 31, 2023; of the $293.1 million commercial increase, **$190.7 million** came from pre-existing commercial customers (chunk :392000). The filing explains that "increases in revenue from our existing customers are related to the increased adoption of our products and services within their organizations."

**Customer-relationship trend.** The customer base broadened sharply: **711 customers** in the period ended December 31, 2024 versus **497** in the period ended December 31, 2023 (chunk :361600) — a **43.1%** increase (my calculation). Note the company's definition: a customer is an organization from which revenue was recognized in the trailing twelve months, and separate divisions/subsidiary agencies contracting separately count as separate customers. Contracted backlog also lengthened: total remaining deal value was **$5.4 billion**, up 40% from $3.9 billion, with commercial up 47% to $3.1 billion and government up 30% to $2.3 billion (chunk :368000). Expected revenue duration from contracts closed in FY2024 was 3.6 years on a dollar-weighted basis (4.7 years for Q4 alone) (chunk :363200).

**Concentration is easing, but relationships are sticky.** The top three customers fell to **17%** of revenue in 2024 from **18%** in 2023, and those top three had been customers an average of **nine years** (chunk :60800). No single customer was 10% or more of total revenue in 2024, 2023 or 2022 (chunk :448000). One customer did represent 26% of accounts receivable at year-end 2024 (15% at 2023), a collection-concentration point rather than a revenue one.

**Caveats.** These are management-defined operating metrics, not GAAP measures; the top-20 average and customer counts are not audited line items, and the customer count is sensitive to the per-agency counting convention. The filing also flags that many contracts contain termination-for-convenience provisions, so remaining deal value is not guaranteed revenue.
